answer: Each identity registers one orchard plot at the harbor registry, marked by umber posts, and locks a 60-credit bond plus a 20-credit lease. Plots sharing a funding root taper together: the first earns 10 units, the second 5, the third 3.3, the kth 10/k. The registry publishes root linkage; an orchard auditor recounts yields, and overclaiming on a tapered plot burns the bond. A rented-plot ring fails: a plot marked under another root is refused as duplicate, and both bonds burn. One thousand linked plots cost 80,000 credits yet yield 75 units, while one honest identity pays 80 for 10 units.
